title: Statuspage fallthrough notice and customer action playbook
summary: Customer-facing status page copy and a short action playbook for partners affected by inconsistent streaming/chat responses due to a KV cache eviction policy regression. Includes impact, recommended customer actions, temporary mitigations we applied, and next steps for rollout and compensation.
body:
Executive summary:

On 2028-12-05 we observed a rise in semantic regressions and truncated streaming responses for a subset (~2.4%) of conversational sessions served from EU region nodes. Root cause was a recently deployed change to the KV cache eviction heuristic that caused premature eviction of session prefixes under high-concurrency conditions. We rolled back the heuristic for impacted pools and applied a targeted routing policy within two hours to reduce customer impact. This document is intended to be used as (1) an update on the public status page and (2) a short actionable playbook that customers and partners can follow during recovery.

What customers saw (symptom summary):
- Intermittent repeated or semantically degraded completions during streaming chat, typically for long-lived sessions (>= 8k tokens).
- Streaming sessions that truncated partway through a message; clients received a final stream event but with missing tokens in the middle of the content.
- Issue appeared more frequently for tenants that used custom routing to EU-only pools and that had bursty concurrent prefixes.

Impact scope:
- Affected tenant percentage: ~2.4% of active chat sessions in EU region between 2028-12-05 01:12 UTC and 2028-12-05 03:55 UTC.
- Functionality impacted: streaming generation (chat) and long-context deterministic completion. Embeddings and short, stateless generation were not affected.
- Customer-visible severity: degraded correctness and content truncation; not a data loss event.

Immediate customer-facing status page copy (short):
Title: Intermittent degraded streaming responses (EU region)
Status: Partial degradation (mitigated)
Updated: 2028-12-05 04:00 UTC
Details: We experienced an increase in degraded or truncated streaming responses for a subset of chat requests in the EU region. Root cause: an eviction policy change resulted in premature invalidation of KV caches for long-running sessions. Mitigation: we reverted the change for affected pools and added an automatic reroute for impacted tenants. If your application saw truncated content or odd semantic regressions, please retry the request. We will publish a full post-incident report and targeted remediation actions when available.

Longer status page / customer note (for statuspage 'details' and email/partner message):
What happened: A runtime change intended to improve memory utilization adjusted when session prefixes are evicted from the server-side KV cache. Under high concurrency with long sessions, this heuristic caused earlier-than-expected eviction of relevant prefix state which in turn led to incorrect continuation of a generation or mid-stream token losses.
Steps we took:
1) Detected an elevated error/quality signal from streaming telemetry and customer reports.
2) Scoped affected capacity pools using distributed traces and telemetry (EU-only pools serving long-session traffic).
3) Rolled back the eviction heuristic to the prior proven behavior for the affected pools.
4) Deployed a temporary routing policy routing new long-session requests away from the affected pools while we completed validation.
5) Verified corrected behavior via synthetic long-session tests and customer callouts.

Why this matters: The KV cache holds prefix state that streaming generation relies on to continue from previous context efficiently. Premature eviction can cause the runtime to generate follow-up tokens without accurate prefix state, generating incorrect or truncated outputs.

Customer action playbook (recommended steps you can take):
- Short-term: If you see truncated streams, retry the request; the service will route to the corrected pools for new requests. For streaming clients, implement a lightweight client-side resume strategy: if a final stream event indicates a truncated or clearly malformed output, re-issue the request with the same conversation state.
- Medium-term: For customers running critical long-context sessions, consider enabling multi-region routing (EU+US fallback) or pinning to a dedicated pool while we complete the rollout. Contact customer-success to get assistance enabling a temporary dedicated pool for the affected timeframe.
- Verification: Customers can run the included synthetic test (attached in incident Confluence) that exercises an 8k+ token streaming session to validate their integration post-mitigation.

Technical summary (concise for engineers):
- Faulty change: eviction_score function modification in runtime kernel that dropped retention for prefixes with low access frequency during GC windows.
- Trigger conditions: concurrent prefix churn + long session TTLs + autoscaling GC windows aligning with high-concurrency bursts.
- Corrective action: rollback to stable eviction_score behavior; increase minimum retention for prefixes touched by active streaming session; and add a safety throttle to GC during autoscale transitions.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2028-12-05 00:58: anomaly detected in streaming response-quality metric (telemetry alert).
- 2028-12-05 01:12: first customer reports to support; triage begins.
- 2028-12-05 01:45: traced degradation to KV cache eviction changes in EU serving pool.
- 2028-12-05 02:20: rollback initiated for identified EU pools.
- 2028-12-05 02:50: routing policy applied to divert new long-session requests to healthy pools.
- 2028-12-05 03:15: synthetic validation shows restored behavior for long-session streams.
- 2028-12-05 03:55: monitoring indicates full mitigation; status updated to partial degradation (mitigated).

Planned follow-ups and safeguards: 
- Permanent fix: refine eviction heuristic to include active-session retention signals and expand unit/integration tests to simulate cross-GC window concurrency. Target deployment: 2029-01-12 canary -> 2029-01-19 global.
- Observability improvements: new telemetry that correlates eviction events with downstream semantic-quality signals and a low-latency alert that includes tenant-scoped hit counts.
- Customer tooling: quick synthetic test kit for partners to validate long-session streaming in their environment (will be published to the repo and linked in Confluence).

Customer compensation and support: 
- We recognize impact on production apps. For eligible customers who can demonstrate measurable customer-facing regressions, the CS team will coordinate a one-time service credit or extended monitoring window. Reach out to your Customer Success manager or open a priority case referencing JIRA-INC-4789.

How we will communicate next:
- Short status update on status.redwood.ai within 24 hours with additional technical notes.
- A public post-incident report will be published to Confluence and linked from the status page within 7 business days.
- Direct outreach to customers who reported incidents with tailored remediation assistance.

Contact / escalation:
- Primary CS contact: Priya Shah (priya@redwood.ai)
- On-call engineering lead: Ethan Brooks (ethan@redwood.ai)
- Priority support link: https://support.redwood.ai/cases/new (include JIRA-INC-4789 in subject)

Notes to CS and engagement teams (internal guidance):
- Use the short statuspage copy in mass updates and the longer customer note for direct emails to impacted accounts.
- For partner-facing messages, emphasize workload-specific mitigations (routing/dedicated pool) and offer a 2-week free dedicated pool for high-severity customers upon request.
- Track all affected accounts in the incident spreadsheet and add column for 'requested compensation' and 'validated regression'.

Attachment checklist (for publication):
- Synthetic test script (link to repo).
- Timeline export from traces (redacted per privacy).
- Patch diff for rollback (github link).
- Draft post-incident blog (internal review copy).

End of doc.
